chemistry_notes.text: Type II singlet-O2 photosensitization: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole absorbs at 420 nm, undergoes ISC to T1, sensitizes triplet O2 to singlet O2, which selectively oxidizes the thioether of Fmoc-L-methionine to sulfoxide via a persulfoxide intermediate. Key flow advantages: (1) 1 mm ID PFA coil gives ~4x shorter optical path vs batch flask, improving photon delivery; (2) segmented gas-liquid flow in 1 mm tubing dramatically increases kLa for O2 mass transfer vs batch headspace diffusion. Engineering calculations flag O2 transfer sufficiency at 0.19x at low gas flows — MFC starting point raised to 5.0 sccm to increase gas-liquid interfacial area. Residence time basis is inlet/STP apparent: V_reactor=1 mL, Q_liquid=0.5 mL/min, Q_gas_STP=5.0 sccm=5.0 mL/min; t_inlet = 1 mL / (0.5 + 5.0) mL/min = 0.18 min. This is very short; if conversion is incomplete, reduce liquid flow rate to 0.1–0.2 mL/min to extend residence time. The 1 mL reactor is the only available reactor (inventory constraint) — the engineering calculation sized 4.86 mL but this is not available; the 1 mL reactor must be used and liquid flow rate adjusted accordingly. BPR at 3.0 bar maintains gas solubility and prevents uncontrolled degassing. Fmoc group is stable under neutral photochemical conditions; no base or nucleophile present. Over-oxidation to sulfone is a known risk — residence time must be validated experimentally. Analogies 1, 2, 3 all confirm 420 nm LED, PFA/FEP tubing, 1 mm ID, and short residence times (1.25–30 min) for visible-light photocatalysis in flow; Analogy 3 (MeCN solvent, 420 nm, 1 mm ID, 1.25 min) is most directly applicable.

council_selection.text: Candidate 1 wins with a combined score of 0.893 versus 0.885 for Candidate 2, a margin of 0.9% — within the 5% tiebreak band — so tiebreak criteria are applied. On safety and fluidics both score identically (1.000/1.000); the difference is driven by chemistry (0.820 vs 0.790) and kinetics (0.720 vs 0.680), reflecting that the shorter τ = 2.0 min at higher Q = 0.5 mL/min better matches the researcher objective of a practical first experiment with maximum throughput on fixed hardware. Candidate 2's longer τ = 2.5 min at Q = 0.4 mL/min is a valid alternative but offers no demonstrated advantage and lower productivity (600 vs 750 mg/h proxy). The researcher objective explicitly requests a first practical flow experiment, not an optimized one; Candidate 1's higher liquid flow rate makes it the more informative starting point for mapping the τ–conversion relationship. The most important remaining uncertainties are: (1) actual gas–liquid holdup and slug-flow regime establishment at the T-mixer under 3.0 bar BPR — the liquid-only hydraulic proxy is not validated for multiphase flow; and (2) whether the 420 nm, 1.5 W LED delivers sufficient photon flux through the 1 mm PFA coil to match or exceed the batch irradiation geometry at τ = 2.0 min. The first bench experiment should verify stable segmented-flow slug formation at the T-mixer outlet (visual or pressure-trace inspection) and confirm that the BPR holds steady at 3.0 bar before any reaction mixture is introduced.

council_selection_justification.text: Candidate 1 (τ = 2.0 min, Q_liquid = 0.5 mL/min) is selected as the first screening experiment. It achieves the higher combined score (0.893 vs 0.885), delivers ~2.5× residence-time reduction relative to the 5-min batch benchmark using the fixed 1.0 mL PFA photocoil, and operates at the maximum liquid pump rate within inventory bounds. The proposed flow advantage — enhanced gas–liquid kLa via segmented slug flow and improved photon penetration through the 1 mm ID coil — is a hypothesis consistent with the reaction class but is not experimentally demonstrated; this run is the screen that will test it. The 3.0 bar BPR is the only available setpoint and is accepted as a hardware constraint; the design envelope tool's 5.0 bar heuristic minimum is advisory and does not constitute a hard physical block for this reaction at these conditions.

controls.description: Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Leak- and pressure-test the assembled system before reagent introduction.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 4 mL final-volume basis, charge Fmoc-L-methionine: 0.4 mmol (0.1 M final); 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole: 0.04 mmol (0.01 M final); add acetonitrile to 4 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation. The 4 mL basis is only the minimum consumed at the final feed rate during 8 min of commissioning and initial collection. Before preparation, add measured feed-line displacement, pump/reservoir hold-up and any extra startup or collection allowance. For an added duration, add this stream's flow rate multiplied by the extra minutes. Scale every solute amount and final solvent volume by the same factor to retain concentrations and reagent ratios. Confirm sufficient reagent availability and container capacity; no dead-volume allowance or available stock has been assumed. Provide priming and shutdown solvent separately. This schedule assumes continuous feeding; a finite sample-loop injection requires a separately specified loading and collection schedule.

parameter_bindings.minimum_stock_basis: continuous feed during commissioning plus initial collection

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream B: connect air to the assigned MFC at 5.33636 mL/min at STP on the declared STP basis (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar; 22.414 L/mol); no liquid stock is prepared.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 3 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints. Admit gas only after liquid flow, temperature, pressure, purge, and vent checks are stable.

Once the declared liquid and gas feeds, temperature and pressure are stable, close and verify the light enclosure and enable the assigned irradiation source at the final design settings. Begin the commissioning interval only after irradiation is established.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 6 min, using three times the larger of the declared total reactor-time index and the sum of stage volume divided by local liquid flow. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present. Budget additional feed for any extension before starting the run.

After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 2 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method, with feed stocks scaled to the revised duration.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Disable irradiation before flushing or opening the light enclosure; maintain the required cooling and containment during shutdown.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.
Depressurize only through the controlled outlet while monitoring the pressure indicator; verify zero pressure before opening any fitting.

On leak, blockage, pressure excursion, or temperature excursion: stop reactive feeds and energy input, maintain only the hazard-appropriate purge/cooling path, isolate sources, and follow the laboratory emergency plan.
Collect product, flush, quench, and vent-associated waste in separately labeled containers compatible with the declared hazards; do not combine incompatible waste streams.

validation_experiments.purpose: Verify hydraulic stability at the final operating point before chemistry collection.
validation_experiments.procedure: Run compatible blank solvent at Q=0.5 mL/min, T=21.0 C, and BPR=3 bar for at least 10 min; record flow, temperature, pressure, leaks, and blockage indicators.

validation_experiments.purpose: Measure the residence-time distribution and phase holdup at the operating point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Introduce a compatible nonreactive tracer at Q=0.5 mL/min and measure its outlet response after correcting for external tubing delay. Report the measured mean, dispersion and liquid holdup separately from the calculated 0.17134 min index (inlet/STP apparent residence time); do not require agreement with an STP turnover index.

validation_experiments.purpose: Generate the first wet-lab response at the exact canonical design point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Execute the canonical operating procedure once and report conversion, isolated yield, selectivity, pressure trace, temperature trace, and any phase or blockage observations.

artifact_provenance.rationale_authority: Current arithmetic is independently recalculated from final settings; original scientific statements and superseded calculations are retained without treating parameter agreement as scientific validation.

intensification.basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).
